summary: Diana L. Eck is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned her B.A. at Smith College, M.A. at SOAS, and Ph.D. at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. Around 1976, she became a professor at Harvard University.

Diana Lange works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Leipzig, Tibet, and Humboldt Universities, with a habilitation from EPHE, she held research posts across Germany before becoming Professor of Central Asian History and Cultures at Humboldt in 2025.

Diane A. Lichtenstein earned her PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1977. In 2005, she was attested as an Adjunct Professor of Anthropology at both Baldwin Wallace University and the Cleveland Institute of Art.

Diane E. Riggs specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at UCLA in 2010 under William M. Bodiford, and later held posts at Kenyon College, Pepperdine University, and Western Michigan University (attested 2017).
Diane L. Howard is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 1982, she was attested as a graduate student at McMaster University, where she studied under supervisor Graeme MacQueen.
Dickwela Piyananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the Catholic University of America, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Siegfried A. Schulz.
Diego Loukota specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a master's degree from Peking University and completed his PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles in 2019.

Dieter B. Kapp specialized in Indology and linguistics, completing his doctorate under Hermann Berger at Heidelberg University. He taught at Heidelberg, held guest professorships in Munich and Berlin, and served as Director of Indology and Tamilistics at Cologne (1990-2006).
Dieter George was an Indologist who held a post at the Prussian State Library from circa 1972 to 1985. In 1985, he was attested as the successor to Wolfgang Voigt.

Dieter Schlingloff is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Göttingen and Humboldt University. He served at the GDR Academy of Sciences, Göttingen, and as ordentlicher Professor at Kiel (1968-1971) and Honorary Professor at Munich (1972-1996).

Dieter Schuh is a Tibetologist who studied at Cologne and Bonn, earning his PhD and Habilitation at Bonn. He served as professor of Tibetology at Bonn (1978-2007) and founded and directed the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was a scholar of Indology and South Asian history who earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania. He held a visiting fellowship at ANU (1963) and was Chair of South Asian History at Heidelberg University (1968-2001).

Dilgo Khyentse was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Shechen Gyaltsap Pema Namgyal and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and later taught numerous prominent Buddhist teachers and scholars.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti is an archaeologist and Indologist educated at the University of Calcutta. He taught archaeology at Calcutta (1965-1977) and Delhi (1977-1990), and was later Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the University of Cambridge (1990-2008).

Dilip Kumar Biswas was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, where he was taught by Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, and later held posts at Visva-Bharati University and the University of Calcutta.

Dilli Raman Regmi was a scholar of history and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Madras and a D.Litt. from Patna University (circa 1939-1961), and taught at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Dina Bangdel was a scholar of history, art history, and Buddhist and religious studies. She held academic posts at Ohio State University from circa 1999 to 2002 and at Virginia Commonwealth University from circa 2002 to 2017.

Dines Andersen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and served there as professor of Indian philology from 1903 to 1927.

Dineschandra Sircar was an Indologist and historian. He served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1961, and held posts at the University of Calcutta as Lecturer (1937) and Carmichael Professor from 1962.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, and was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University in 1998.
